title: Extensions of arbitrary unipotent affine groups are unipotent
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Unipotent means admitting a closed group immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] into some $\mathcal U_{n,k}\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$, $n\geq1$ [def-sc-general-linear-group], where $\mathcal U_{n,k}(A)$ consists of upper triangular matrices with diagonal entries $1$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Let $N\subseteq E$ be normal and let $q:E\to Q$ represent the fppf quotient $E/N$ [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]: the represented sheaf is the sheafification of $A\mapsto E(A)/N(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings, and $N$ is the scheme-theoretic kernel of $q$. If $N$ and $Q$ are unipotent, then $E$ is unipotent. No smoothness, connectedness, commutativity, centrality or perfectness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 14.7, printed p.282, extension clause, with Theorem 14.5(a),(b), pp.281--282; its proof refers to Proposition 6.45.

proof.text: The quotient in [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry], applied to the given closed normal subgroup $N\subseteq E$, represents the same fppf sheaf as $Q$. The unique representing isomorphism identifies the maps from $E$, since both maps send a point to its coset. Thus the given $q:E\to Q$ is faithfully flat on coordinate algebras, with scheme-theoretic kernel $N$. This uses no smoothness or connectedness.

source.place: Section 6.45, printed p.135; quotient interpretation in Propositions 5.43 and 5.45, pp.109--110.

proof.text: Let $V\ne0$ be any finite-dimensional rational $E$-representation. Write $c_V:V\to V\otimes_k k[E]$ for its coaction using [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary]. Restrict to $N$ and choose a basis of $V$. Since $N$ has the closed unitriangular embedding in the hypothesis, [lem-sfb-unitriangular-subgroup-rational-fixed-vector] gives $v\ne0$ fixed by $N(A)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. The dictionary identifies this condition with the restricted coaction $v\mapsto v\otimes1$.

source.place: Section 6.45, p.135; Theorem 14.5(b) implies (a), pp.281--282; Remark 4.1, p.84.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-central-kernel-cyclic-representation-descent] with $H=E$, $G=Q$, $K=N$, the faithfully flat $q$ of step 1 and the vector $v$ of step 2. Its hypotheses are exactly satisfied, including invariance over every algebra. The smallest $E$-subcomodule $W\subseteq V$ containing $v$ is nonzero and finite-dimensional, its $N$-action is trivial, and its $E$-action descends to a rational $Q$-action. In particular, for each $A$ and $e\in E(A)$, the action on $W_A$ is the action of $q_A(e)\in Q(A)$. Centrality of $N$ is not required by the cited statement.

source.place: Section 6.45, p.135, using Lemma 5.15 and Theorem 5.13, pp.101--102.

proof.text: Choose a basis of $W$ and apply [lem-sfb-unitriangular-subgroup-rational-fixed-vector] to its descended $Q$-representation. Here $\dim W\geq1$ and the required closed embedding of $Q$ is part of the hypothesis. Obtain $w\ne0$ fixed by every $Q(A)$. The pullback identity in step 3 gives $e(w\otimes1)=q_A(e)(w\otimes1)=w\otimes1$ for every $A$ and $e\in E(A)$. The image of $w$ in $V$ is nonzero, so every nonzero finite-dimensional rational $E$-representation has a nonzero vector fixed over every algebra.

Induct on $d=\dim V$ to construct a full flag of rational $E$-submodules with trivial successive quotients. For $d=0$ take the empty flag. For $d>0$, step 4 supplies a fixed $w\ne0$, so $L=kw$ has coaction $w\mapsto w\otimes1$. If $\pi:V\to V/L$, the map $(\pi\otimes1)c_V$ kills $L$ and hence defines the quotient coaction on $V/L$; its counit and coassociativity follow by composing the identities for $c_V$ with $\pi$. Apply the induction hypothesis in dimension $d-1$, and take inverse images of that flag, preceded by $0\subset L$. This gives the full flag and its trivial successive quotient actions. These operations are valid over every algebra: each vector-space exact sequence splits linearly before tensoring. The representation/coaction correspondence is [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary].

source.place: Proposition 14.3, p.280, and Theorem 14.5(a) implies (b), p.281; explicit flag induction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-subgroup-representation-kernel] to $G=E$ and its trivial closed normal subgroup (the identity is cut out by the augmentation ideal of $k[E]$). Obtain $d\geq1$ and $r:E\to\operatorname{GL}_{d,k}$ with trivial scheme-theoretic kernel. For every $A$, if $r_A(x)=r_A(y)$, then $r_A(y^{-1}x)=I_d$, and the stated kernel equality gives $y^{-1}x=1$. Thus $r_A$ is injective for all $A$. By [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-faithful-closed-immersion], $r$ is a closed immersion; both groups are affine of finite type over the arbitrary field $k$.

source.place: Theorem 14.5(a) implies (b), p.281; Corollary 5.19, p.103, and Corollary 3.35, p.75.

proof.text: Apply the flag of step 5 to this faithful $r$, and choose a basis adapted to it. For every algebra $A$, flag preservation forces all entries below the diagonal of $r_A(e)$ to vanish, and triviality on each one-dimensional quotient forces each diagonal entry to be $1$. These are identities of regular functions: evaluate also at the universal point $e=\mathrm{id}_{k[E]}$. Hence the conjugated representation factors through $\mathcal U_{d,k}$. It is a closed immersion into that subgroup: the surjection $k[\operatorname{GL}_d]\to k[E]$ factors through $k[\mathcal U_d]$, so the latter map to $k[E]$ is still surjective, exactly the affine closed-immersion criterion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This is the asserted unitriangular closed embedding over $k$.

source.place: Theorem 14.5(a) implies (b), p.281, with the affine closed-immersion criterion.

proof_origin.place: Section 6.45, printed p.135, assembled with Theorem 14.5(a),(b), printed pp.281--282. The flag induction and the affine factorization are written out.
